function: Joint learned control of UAV 3D movement and IoT-device transmit power on ground-to-air links, minimizing average age of information and energy (p. 7).
system: Ground-to-air links, scalar antenna gain (no MIMO, no RIS); 1 UAV, 20 IoT devices (synthetic), 1-4 UAVs (real city); 5.9 GHz V2I (pp. 4, 6, 9, 12).
method: Deep reinforcement learning with actor-critic networks (TD3, PPO, SAC), trained online by interaction with a simulated environment; reward combines AoI, energy and constraint penalty (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Custom simulator, free-space gain g0*G0/d^2 (Eq. 9); synthetic 1 km region and real downtown building map as no-fly zones; no 3GPP model or measurements (pp. 6, 9, 12).
test_conditions: Training and execution in the same scenario, random UAV start positions; separate training curves per setting (IoT density, kappa, 1-4 UAVs); no unseen-scenario test (pp. 11-12).
baselines: Learned: DDPG. Non-learned: random strategy, PSO and GA solved per time slot; also compares TD3, PPO and SAC with each other (pp. 13-14).
metrics: Average AoI, cumulative reward, unserved IoT devices, average energy consumption of UAVs and IoT devices, inference time expression (pp. 10-15).
complexity: Symbolic inference time only (Table III, p. 15): PSO L_P*P*T_F, GA L_G*Q*T_F, DRL T_N, with T_N assumed approximately T_F; no FLOPs, parameters or measured runtime.
openness: Only a GitHub link for the dynamic resource-allocation procedure (p. 15, footnote 1): https://github.com/ustb-yaxi/Dynamic-procedure-of-resource-allocation.git; code and data not stated as released.
q1_support: p. 6: "g0 denotes the channel power gain at the reference" - Eq. 9 defines a custom free-space gain h = g0 G0 / d^2; no 3GPP TR 38.901, TR 38.811, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used, so the criterion is not met.
q2_support: p. 11: "the initial locations of the UAV in the above DRL simulations during both the training and execution phases" - each setting is trained and tested in its own scenario; no trained model is tested on an unseen scenario or adapted to one.
q3_support: p. 14: "TD3, PPO, and SAC all outperform DDPG" (learned baseline, average AoI in Fig. 15); p. 14: "is inferior to that of the proposed DRL algorithms" (non-learned PSO, GA, random strategy).
q4_support: p. 15: "TN ≈ TF , the time lengths of an inference for PSO and GA are" - Table III gives only symbols (PSO L_P*P*T_F, GA L_G*Q*T_F, DRL T_N); no value, order, FLOPs, parameters or measured runtime for the DRL policy.
q5_support: p. 15: "can be viewed at https://github.com/ustb-yaxi/Dynamic" - footnote 1 links a repository for the dynamic procedure of the results; the paper does not say that code or data are released, and no public channel dataset is used.
notes: Included under the aerial-link rule: the DRL action holds UAV movement and IoT power variation (p. 7, Eq. 20), so a physical-layer decision (transmit power) is learned jointly with the trajectory; area 6. Borderline: the main objective is AoI and UAV trajectory (above physical layer), so the reviewer should confirm. Abstract and p. 15 (VII-A3) claim transferability and good generalization under various city topologies, but no test of a trained model on an unseen topology is reported. The link in footnote 1 has a hyphen after Dynamic at a line break (p. 15); repository content not checked.
